_README: Edge-Function deploy ledger (B-178 / CUL-135). One entry per deployable function. `fingerprint` = the sha256 of the function's shipping import-closure (index.ts + every local .ts it inlines) last acknowledged for deploy — computed by guards/edgeFunctionDeploy.test.ts, which FAILS THE BUILD when a function drifts from its recorded fingerprint without a reasoned acknowledgment. Statuses: `deployed` (fingerprint confirmed live), `pending` (a deploy is owed OR the live state is unverified — see the entry's `reason`), `hold` (deliberately not deployed — e.g. B-494). `pending`/`hold` require a `reason`. After deploying a function, set its `fingerprint` to the current value (the guard's failure message prints it) with status `deployed`. This ledger records intent; it does NOT prove a deploy happened — see docs/edge-deploy-runbook.md § Deploy ledger.
_seed: Seeded 2026-08-19 (CUL-135). Fingerprints are the current main closures at ledger creation. Live-vs-main was NOT verified per-function (the live artifact is a bundle, not a source closure, and this guard is token-free by design), so no function is seeded `deployed`: generate-report is the one confirmed `hold` (B-494); every other function is `pending` (baseline). Each converts to `deployed` on its next verified deploy-from-main, or via the live reconciliation follow-on (CUL-541).

generate-report.reason: FIFTH COLD READ — the unattested clause now NAMES THE CAPABILITY. The two arms keep ONE SHAPE (<fact>; Culprit cannot say <unknown>), and the parallel-shape test caught the first cut of this change breaking it. Hedging it changes every trial report carrying a vet name, with or without a window change; filed on CUL-1047. Also measured and filed: the qual span class is emitted three times and HAS NO CSS RULE at all, so every qualifier it wraps renders at full weight beside the facts (CUL-1048). FIVE ROUNDS, STOPPED: each produced a distinct real finding, and what is left is two report-wide changes that belong to the style pass and the cold-read remediation track, not to this PR. — FOURTH COLD READ — THE WINDOW CHANGE IS NOW ITS OWN ROW, and this is the first STRUCTURAL repair of the four. Three rounds of copy fixes fought what turned out to be a layout defect: given the repaired page the reviewer still attributed the extension to the named vet at ~75-80% and diagnosed it as 'a render defect, not a data defect — it separates them in the data and merges them on the page'. Four mechanisms, every one a property of ONE JOINED PARAGRAPH rather than of any sentence in it: identity.join(' ') put the change and 'Trial directed by <name>' nine words apart in a single kv cell; 'a vet' narrows to a class with exactly one named member on the page; the disclaimer came BEFORE the name so the name back-filled the slot it opened; and a bolded claim sat beside an unbolded refusal. Its own labelled 'Window change' row answers three of the four at once, and it is far smaller than the report-wide row split the reviewer proposes in general: THE ROW EXISTS ONLY WHEN A WINDOW HAS MOVED, so every report that never had one renders byte-identically. It sits AFTER the Trial row on purpose — 'reverse them and the disclaimer is at least the reader's final state'. It also un-camouflages the one hedge that changes management: the same read measured the block at ~40% epistemics and found a reader pattern-matches sentences opening with 'Culprit' as boilerplate by the fourth, so 'over-hedging is the delivery mechanism for the attribution failure, not a separate complaint about it'. Two tests pin same-row adjacency and order; mutation-proven by putting the clause back in the paragraph. STILL OUT OF SCOPE and routed to the PM: splitting the whole Trial row into labelled rows, which is report-wide. — BRIEF C RULED (a) 2026-09-17 — THE ABSENCE IS NOW STATED, a deliberate deviation from §5.1's 'the clause is simply absent'. With the box unticked the row said nothing, and two independent cold reads measured the same result: silence next to a named vet is read as concurrence (~55-60%), INVISIBLY, because a cold reader cannot see a sentence that is missing. The class: absence of an attribution disclaimer was being rendered AS attribution — the two-sided rule's own hazard inverted, landing hardest on the record deserving the most scepticism, because the weaker record got the less hedged page. The unattested arm now renders 'Culprit cannot say who asked for the change.' It does NOT break the rule §5.1 exists to enforce, which forbids rendering the absence as 'the owner did this on their own' — a claim about the OWNER. This is a claim about the RECORD and attributes the change to nobody, so §8.8 ('with the box unchecked, no clause attributes the change to anyone') still holds with it on the page, asserted as such. The two arms are parallel by design — same subject, differing only in what is unknown — so a clinician meets one sentence shape across two reports rather than a presence and an absence. It fires on the window move, not on whether a vet is named: conditioning it on vet_name would make a sentence ABOUT THE CHANGE appear and vanish on a field that is not about the change, and the finding did not need a name to land. Six tests, four mutations (silence restored, owner blamed, arms swapped, verb echo).
